Use case: identity-preserve. Production game animation sheet, NOT concept art. Edit the approved cockpit/pilot reference into a complete talking animation in the clean 16-bit comic illustration style of the Decker style reference. The cockpit reference defines THIS pilot's identity, clothing, pose, ship interior and colored instrument lighting; the Decker portrait defines ink outlines, simplified cel-shaded pixel clusters and the rendering style ONLY. Never copy Decker's blond hair or facial features onto a different pilot. One fixed camera facing the pilot INSIDE their ship, seated at the controls: full head/hair comfortably below the top of frame, shoulders, chest, both arms/hands in their original pose, black harness and dashboard/control stick foreground. No floating heads. A coherent fully painted cockpit interior behind the pilot, not a portrait pasted over scenery. Keep cabin structure, lighting, head position, identity, torso, hands and console PIXEL-STABLE across frames. Mouth/eyelids are the only animation. Output one sheet in exactly FOUR columns by TWO rows, eight equal landscape cells, each cell aspect ratio 3:2, overall sheet 3:1. Cells fully illustrate the same fixed cockpit composition. Outside/gaps transparent; no baked checkerboard. Eight frames in reading order: 0 closed-mouth neutral eyes open; 1 wide A mouth; 2 E/teeth speaking mouth; 3 rounded O mouth; 4 small pursed U mouth; 5 F/V lip/teeth mouth; 6 small open speaking mouth; 7 closed-mouth blink. No pose change, no head turn, no body sway, no camera movement, no character scale changes, no captions, no lettering, no labels, no dividers, no new characters. Crisp high-quality 16-bit arcade comic art matching the new dialogue portraits, NOT photorealism or 3D. The pilot must look like their reference, including skin tone, hair, beard, glasses, clothing and signature accessories. Preserve generous safe margins around the complete head and hands.
THIS PILOT IS COLE: same actual likeness as the seated cockpit reference, blue eyes, short swept brown hair with closely trimmed sides, thick close-trimmed dark beard, broad brow and jaw, olive green flight suit and hood collar, green cockpit lights. His face must remain recognizably the approved cockpit man; avoid a narrow long face, tall cartoon quiff or generic pretty-boy likeness. Hands remain on the controls.
